name: What accessibility features are most important in an aging-in-place tiny home?
description: Key features include zero-step entries, wide doorways, open floor plans, roll-in showers, grab bars, comfort-height toilets, and accessible kitchen layouts.

mainEntity.name: What accessibility features are most important in an aging-in-place tiny home?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most important accessibility features for an aging-in-place tiny home often include zero-step entries, wider doorways (at least 36 inches), and an open floor plan to accommodate mobility devices. Bathrooms are crucial, requiring roll-in showers with seating, grab bars, and comfort-height toilets. Kitchens benefit from adjustable-height counters, pull-out shelves, and easy-to-reach appliances. Lever-style door handles, rocker light switches, and ample, glare-free lighting throughout the home also significantly enhance safety and ease of use.
